newsitem.title: USA: Aide to Arafat says talks with Israel go on.
newsitem.headline: Aide to Arafat says talks with Israel go on.

text.p: Israeli-Palestinian talks to end an outburst of violence went into the night on Tuesday but it was too early to say whether a U.S.-sponsored emergency summit would end in agreement, an adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said.

"All I can say is the talks are still continuing and there is an American effort ... and let's wait and see," Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters. Officials said low-level talks were taking place ahead of the summit's scheduled conclusion on Wednesday.

Asked if Arafat would meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu again on Tuesday night after a three-hour meeting during the day, Abu Rdainah said: "Until now I can't say yes or no. We are still in the process of negotiations and we'll wait and see."
An Israeli government source said earlier that a late-night meeting was likely.

U.S. President Bill Clinton summoned the Israeli and Palestinian leaders to the summit to try to get peace moves back on track following four days of gun battles and clashes that claimed the lives of 72 people.
